LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 6.1.1 PRONUNCIATION AND VOCABULARY

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.1: Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, part of Strand 6 in Grade 6 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why do we put emphasis on some words and not others? 2. How can you vary your voice to convey different meanings?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. say sounds, words, phrases, and sentences with the sounds /f/, /v/ and /əʊ/,

2. say tongue twisters with the sounds /f/ and /v/ and /əʊ/,

3. watch a video of a dialogue on work ethics and imitate the use of stress and intonation by the speakers,

4. recite a choral verse, with peers,

5. sing songs featuring stress and intonation,

6. form sentences using the following expressions: fixed 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. say sounds, words, phrases, and sentences with the sounds /f/, /v/ and /əʊ/,
2. say tongue twisters with the sounds /f/ and /v/ and /əʊ/,
3. watch a video of a dialogue on work ethics and imitate the use of stress and intonation by the speakers,
4. recite a choral verse, with peers,
5. sing songs featuring stress and intonation,
6. form sentences using the following expressions: fixed 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication: The learner’s ability to speak clearly and effectively is enhanced through practice and saying

tongue twisters with the sounds /f/, /v/ and /əʊ/.

• Self-efficacy: The learner’s ability to analyse is developed when they give their views as they form sentences

using the given expressions.
